title: Priority watermarks: connection slimming and downstream shedding for regional outages
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: During cross-region incidents we observe connection pool saturation to Redis and primary DB replicas which causes cascading client timeouts and increased tail latency. Existing strategies (global hedging, simple circuit breakers) are insufficient for multi-tenant pools where a handful of noisy tenants can starve the pool. This ticket defines an implementation for prioritized connection trimming ("connection slimming"), tenant watermarks, and coordinated downstream shedding for Redis/Kafka/DB to maintain SLOs for high-priority traffic while degrading lower-priority work gracefully.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Implement per-tenant dynamic watermark thresholds (low/medium/high) enforced by the connection manager; thresholds adjustable via Console
2) When pool saturation exceeds X% sustained for Y seconds, trigger connection slimming to reduce per-tenant allocations to watermark levels and prevent global exhaustion
3) Integrate a downstream shedding handshake: services may indicate 'can-shed' boolean in request metadata and receive a 429-suggested response when shedding is active
4) Expose observability: per-tenant pool usage, denied-connections metric, watermark state changes, and shed decisions in Console dashboard and tracing
5) Run chaos injection (region network latency) in staging and demonstrate high-priority request P95 latency stays within SLO while low-priority error rate increases predictably
6) Backfill migration guide and automated rollout with canary to avoid single-region full rollout failures
proposed_solution: We will extend the connection pool manager with a lightweight priority-aware allocator. Each tenant has a soft and hard watermark defined by usage history and SLA tier. On steady-state, soft watermarks are used to fairly distribute connections. When pool saturation is detected (configurable: default 85% for 30s), the allocator enters 'slim' mode and immediately trims soft allocations toward the hard watermark, freeing connections for higher-priority tenants. Concurrently, an API-level shedding protocol signals downstream components (Redis client wrapper, Kafka producer, DB client) to reject or downgrade non-essential operations. Circuit breaker state transitions will include a 'slim' reason code so fallbacks choose degraded paths (e.g., read-only cache, local KV snapshot). We'll add telemetry and runbook links so on-call can safely escalate. Implementation will be feature-flagged and controllable per-cluster and per-region via Console.

2026-03-12: Addressing edge case where tenant connection pool churn causes heartbeat timeouts; working on exponential smoothing for watermark calculations.
